title: Rivals Circle an Out-of-Touch Prabowo
gist: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto's approval has collapsed from 75% to 37% in eight months amid protests turned deadly, with gangster militia GRIB Jaya deployed against demonstrators and rivals (Jokowi, Dedi Mulyadi) already positioning for succession well before the scheduled 2029 election.

insights.claim: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto's approval rating fell from 75% in December 2025 to 37% in August 2026, according to Tempo Data Science polling, driven by dissatisfaction over high prices and limited job opportunities.
insights.speaker: Joseph Rachman
insights.so_what: A collapse of this magnitude in eight months signals acute political instability risk in Southeast Asia's largest economy, raising the odds of policy paralysis, populist reversals, or an early leadership change ahead of 2029.
insights.quote: It was at 37 percent in August compared to 75 percent last December, according to a recent poll by Tempo Data Science.
insights.locator: Thugs come out as government popularity slips

insights.claim: A pro-Prabowo gangster-political organization called GRIB Jaya (United Indonesian People's Movement), led by Rosario de Marcal ('Hercules'), deployed armed men in trucks during the August 27 Jakarta protests, and a 60-year-old shopkeeper, Bambang Setiawan, died after being attacked by the group even though GRIB Jaya denies responsibility.
insights.speaker: Joseph Rachman
insights.so_what: State-linked militia violence against protesters is a classic late-stage authoritarian-drift signal; investors in Indonesian assets should watch for further crackdowns, capital flight, or a legitimacy crisis that could disrupt policy continuity.
insights.locator: Thugs come out as government popularity slips

insights.claim: Indonesian gangster groups have a long history of acting as informal arms of the state during political crises, a pattern the author says was on blatant display for the first time since Indonesia's 1998 democratization during the August 2026 unrest.
insights.speaker: Joseph Rachman
insights.so_what: Recognizing this historical pattern helps investors read future unrest: militia mobilization is a signal the state is using extralegal muscle rather than reform to manage discontent, often a precursor to further instability.
insights.quote: Indonesia’s gangsters have a long history of acting as arms of the state in a crisis.
insights.locator: Thugs come out as government popularity slips

insights.claim: Former Indonesian President Joko Widodo ('Jokowi'), whose implicit endorsement was central to Prabowo's 2024 election win, has begun signaling discontent after being sidelined by Prabowo, including a rare interview on the Prabowo-critical podcast Bocor Alus and a video appearance alongside pro-Jokowi organizer Budi Arie Setiadi who floated the idea of elections coming before 2029.
insights.speaker: Joseph Rachman
insights.so_what: Watch for a Jokowi-backed break from Prabowo; if the alliance that installed Prabowo unravels, it raises tail risk of an early leadership transition or coalition realignment that could roil Indonesian markets.
insights.locator: Thugs come out as government popularity slips

insights.claim: Budi Arie Setiadi compared Indonesia's current unrest to 1998, when riots abruptly ended the 31-year rule of Suharto (Prabowo's former father-in-law), while Jokowi sat silently without contradicting him, though Budi later apologized and downplayed the remarks.
insights.speaker: Joseph Rachman
insights.so_what: Explicit 1998-collapse comparisons circulating among pro-Jokowi figures, even if later walked back, indicate elite factions are actively war-gaming a premature end to Prabowo's presidency.
insights.locator: Thugs come out as government popularity slips

insights.claim: West Java Governor Dedi Mulyadi, elected last year under Prabowo's own party, now leads polls as the preferred next president, having built a highly effective social-media presence that contrasts with Prabowo's image as slow and out of touch (e.g., visibly slower to visit earthquake victims than Dedi, who filmed himself flying in for relief efforts).
insights.speaker: Joseph Rachman
insights.so_what: A rival from within Prabowo's own party leading presidential polls this early signals intra-coalition fragmentation; his political rise is worth tracking as a proxy for shifting elite alignment in Indonesia.
insights.locator: Thugs come out as government popularity slips

insights.claim: Thailand's new law, effective from the last Friday in August 2026, speeds deportation of foreigners who disrupt public order, disrespect Thai culture, work illegally, or commit crimes, part of a broader 2025-2026 crackdown on visa runs and 'nominee' companies used by foreigners to bypass land/business ownership rules.
insights.speaker: Joseph Rachman
insights.so_what: Tightening foreign-ownership workaround enforcement in Thailand raises compliance risk for foreign investors and expats using nominee structures; expect further scrutiny of gray-market business arrangements.

insights.claim: Myanmar's junta leader Min Aung Hlaing is on a successful diplomatic tear post sham January 2026 elections, securing his third major ASEAN-adjacent engagement (after Laos and Thailand) with a Vietnamese foreign minister visit that discussed boosting bilateral trade to $1 billion from 2025's $591 million, despite Myanmar remaining formally excluded from ASEAN.
insights.speaker: Joseph Rachman
insights.so_what: Myanmar's junta is steadily normalizing regional relations despite ASEAN's official exclusion policy, suggesting sanctions/isolation strategies are eroding and trade with Myanmar could re-expand.

insights.claim: Malaysian PM Anwar Ibrahim announced cost-of-living relief (fuel subsidy quota increases, school/small-trader funds, free AI app access for those aged 18-30) funded partly by seized illegal-activity funds, even as his coalition has performed poorly in recent state elections despite ~6% GDP growth, and reporting suggests he may delay elections until 2027 hoping popularity recovers.
insights.speaker: Joseph Rachman
insights.so_what: Strong Malaysian GDP growth is not translating into political support, a disconnect worth watching as a leading indicator that headline macro strength can mask cost-of-living-driven political risk elsewhere in the region.

themes.theme: Southeast Asia's haze crisis and plantation economics

insights.claim: Indonesian forest and peatland fires in Borneo and Sumatra have already affected 14.5 million people, with talk of declaring a national emergency; air quality index readings exceeded 1,000 in Central Kalimantan and 500 in Kuching, Malaysia on Aug. 31, far above the 300 threshold for 'avoid all outdoor activity.'
insights.speaker: Joseph Rachman
insights.so_what: Severe, worsening annual haze events are a recurring regional externality tied to plantation agriculture; expect periodic disruption to logistics, tourism, and public health costs across Indonesia and Malaysia during burning season.

insights.claim: The Indonesian haze crisis is structurally tied to the expansion of plantation agriculture into rainforest areas, and despite Prabowo revoking permits for six companies (with 42 under investigation) for illegal land-clearing fires, a serious policy shift is unlikely because the government is simultaneously promoting its own state-led plantations.
insights.speaker: Joseph Rachman
insights.so_what: Because the state has a commercial stake in plantation expansion, enforcement against land-clearing fires will likely remain symbolic rather than structural, meaning haze-driven agricultural commodity supply risk (palm oil, pulp) will recur annually.
insights.quote: However, with the government promoting its own state-led plantations, a serious shift in policy seems unlikely.
